validation_holdout.statement: Whole physical drives are held out (sessions grouped as evaluation.group_into_drives groups them). Drives are taken in a seeded random order: first, while an operating mode the model will score (at least MIN_CALIBRATION_SAMPLES independent windows) is missing from validation, the drive adding the most missing modes; then drives in order until validation holds validation_fraction of the windows. A drive is skipped when taking it would put more than twice that fraction in validation, leave no drive to train on, or leave a scored mode with fewer than MIN_CALIBRATION_SAMPLES independent training windows. With one drive (or none eligible) the validation set is a contiguous tail block, gapped by one window length.

corpus.split_rule: evaluation = newest physical drive (D6, A02.1); calibration = the calibration picker's own rule (newest healthy, then mode coverage, one session per drive) limited to 2 drives (D5, D3); training = the other 3 drives (D1, D2, D4). The automatic pickers take 3 calibration + up to 3 evaluation drives, which on 6 drives leaves 1 training drive and every IF mode under the non-overridable min_training_drives_per_mode=3.
